story: Alex’s fingers drummed the tabletop, each beat echoing in the quiet café. He glanced at the door every few seconds, as if expecting someone to call his name. His stomach tightened, a flutter beneath his ribs that wouldn’t settle. He kept picking at the edge of his napkin, tearing it into smaller pieces without really noticing. When the barista called his order, he nearly jumped, voice coming out too high. He left without finishing his drink, the half-empty cup left behind as he hurried out into the uncertain afternoon.

Alex’s hands trembled as he turned the key in the door, the hallway stretching long behind him. He checked the locks twice, then stood by the window, eyes fixed on the quiet street. Every distant car seemed to draw closer, and he pressed his palms to his chest, feeling it rise and fall too quickly. He chose a seat in the back corner of the room, shoulders hunched, scanning for exits. When the lights dimmed, he flinched, his breath catching as if he’d forgotten something important outside.

Alex stared at the closed office door, fingers tightening around the handle. His heartbeat thudded, loud and rapid, each beat echoing in the quiet hallway. He took a shaky breath and shifted his weight from one foot to the other, the cold tile pressing through his shoes. Twice, he lifted his hand to knock and let it fall back to his side. The stack of papers in his other hand crinkled under his grip. Finally, he pressed the door open just enough to slip inside, avoiding the gaze of anyone nearby.
